provenance_audit.summary: All four submitted values are 0.0, traceable to the first analysis run on delphes_output.root — a Delphes output from Pythia8 events where the SUSY cascade was broken (chi10 stable in the LHE header SLHA, no chi10→gamma+gravitino decay, hence no hard photons or real MET). The agent correctly diagnosed this as wrong and spent ~40 minutes patching the LHE SLHA to enable proper T5Wg decays. The corrected Delphes run on events_10k_T5Wg.hepmc (with verified SUSY decays: 479/500 test events had hard photons) reached only 47.57% before the 95-minute session timed out. No corrected values were ever computed.

histogram_T5Wg.yaml/T5Wg_1750_1700.source: First bin/run-analysis call on data/delphes_output.root (Delphes output from events without SUSY cascade decays). 0 events passed MET>300 GeV because gravitinos deposited in HCAL and chi10 was stable (no gamma+gravitino decay). Agent diagnosed this as broken and was actively correcting it when the session ended.
issues: Values are from a pipeline the agent explicitly identified as broken (no SUSY decays)
Corrected Delphes run reached only 47.57% before session timeout
Analysis was never re-run on corrected events

overrule.reason: The 0.0 values are genuine outputs of the agent's (broken) pipeline, not fabricated or leaked. The agent was working to correct them but ran out of time. No overrule needed — the submitted zeros simply score poorly against the reference.
overrule.score_policy: Score as submitted; the zeros reflect an incomplete run, not fraud.
overrule.evidence: Session logs show agent diagnosed MET=0 issue, traced it to stable chi10 in LHE SLHA, implemented LHE patching fix, verified correct SUSY decays in 500-event test sample, and was running corrected Delphes when session ended at 47.57%.

trajectory.summary: Agent built a full MG5→Pythia8→Delphes→analysis pipeline for T5Wg gluino pair production but spent most of its 95-minute session debugging why the SUSY cascade wasn't producing photons or MET. It correctly identified three nested issues (chi10 stable in LHE SLHA, missing MODSEL block, charge conjugation for chi1-) and built an LHE header patcher to fix all of them. The corrected pipeline was verified on a 500-event sample (479/500 events with hard photons) but the final Delphes run reached only 48% before timeout, leaving the results at 0.0 from the broken first attempt.
trajectory.planning: Initially well-structured: created simulation directories, wrote SLHA, proc_card, shower driver, and analysis script in parallel with MG5 generation. However, the agent did not allocate enough time budget for the pipeline or prioritize getting any answer over a perfect one. It could have submitted partial results from the 500-event corrected test sample rather than leaving zeros.
trajectory.tool_use: Competent use of MG5, Pythia8 Python API, Delphes, Prospino, and uproot/awkward. Good use of background tasks for long-running simulation jobs. The agent correctly used bin/record-quantity for the ledger (cross section 2.5 fb NLO, luminosity 35.9 fb^-1, trigger efficiency 0.943). However, too many speculative status checks and sleep-poll loops consumed context and wall time.
trajectory.scientific_judgment: Strong physics understanding throughout. Correctly set up T5Wg spectrum (gluino 1750, chi10/chi1+ 1700, massless gravitino). Correctly identified Prospino NLO cross section (2.5 fb). Identified gravitino-in-HCAL problem immediately from MET distributions. Traced the root cause through Pythia8's SLHA override hierarchy (LHE header > external SLHA file). Understood MODSEL's role in activating SUSY processing. The charge conjugation fix for chi1- was particularly astute.
trajectory.honesty_and_reporting: Agent was honest about the broken state — explicitly noted 'MET is 0 for all events' and diagnosed the cause. However, report.md was never filled in and remained as the empty template. The agent did not flag the submitted 0.0 values as known-broken or attempt to submit corrected partial results.
strengths: Correct identification and diagnosis of three nested SUSY decay issues in Pythia8/LHE SLHA handling
Creative LHE header patching approach to inject decay tables that Pythia8 reads from the LHE rather than fighting the override hierarchy
Proper NLO cross section from Prospino (2.5 fb) and correctly populated ledger
Well-structured vectorized analysis code using awkward arrays with correct ST_gamma binning and overflow handling
Verification of fixed pipeline on small test samples before committing to full run

creative_moves.description: Patching the LHE file header SLHA directly to inject MODSEL, gluino decay channels (including chi1- charge conjugate), chi10→gamma+gravitino, and chi1+→W+gravitino — rather than fighting Pythia8's SLHA override hierarchy where the LHE header always wins.
creative_moves.evidence: Agent wrote patch_lhe_slha.py that modifies the SLHA block inside the LHE header. Test on 20 events: 'chi10=10, gravitinos=11, 9 hard photons in 10 events'. Full 10k run: 0 failures, 479/500 with hard photons pT>300 GeV.

creative_moves.description: Extracting partial events from an in-progress Pythia8 HepMC file (30k/50k done) to start Delphes early, saving ~10 minutes of wall time.
creative_moves.evidence: Agent extracted 10k events from events_v2.hepmc while Pythia8 was still writing, then ran Delphes on the truncated file.

stuck_points.description: Spent ~25 minutes on initial MG5 setup issues: wrong dynamical_scale_choice, default MSSM masses instead of custom SLHA, difficulty driving generate_events interactively.
stuck_points.evidence: Three separate MG5 runs (proc_card rewrites, manual param_card copy, Python MadEvent driver) before getting correct 50k events at m_gluino=1750 GeV.

stuck_points.description: First Delphes run OOM-killed at 40% processing the full 2.6 GB events.hepmc (old HepMC format without proper vertex records).
stuck_points.evidence: Agent used the old-format events.hepmc (no V records) instead of events_v2.hepmc. After OOM, extracted 10k events from v2 and re-ran successfully.

stuck_points.description: Agent did not submit partial results from the 500-event corrected test sample when the final Delphes run was clearly going to run out of time.
stuck_points.evidence: The 500-event test showed correct physics (479/500 with hard photons). Running analysis on delphes_500.root (which exists in run_delphes_001) with appropriate normalization would have produced non-zero results, far better than the submitted 0.0.

issues.label: PREMATURE_SURRENDER
issues.description: Agent left submitted results at 0.0 from the known-broken pipeline rather than attempting to extract partial results from the corrected 500-event or partial ~4800-event Delphes outputs.
issues.evidence: delphes_500.root (500 events with correct SUSY decays) and the partial delphes_T5Wg.root (160 MB, ~48% of 10k events) both existed but were never analyzed. The agent's analysis.py could have been run on either with adjusted normalization.

issues.label: INEFFICIENT_WAITING
issues.description: Multiple sleep-poll loops and redundant status checks for Pythia8 and Delphes consumed wall time and context tokens across the 246-turn session.
issues.evidence: Repeated 'tail -3 shower.log' and 'sleep 15/30/60' patterns throughout the session. Agent could have used background tasks more efficiently.

issues.label: INCOMPLETE_SEARCH
issues.description: Agent did not check whether Pythia8's LHE SLHA override behavior was documented before spending significant time debugging it experimentally.
issues.evidence: The LHE-header-overrides-external-SLHA behavior is well-documented in Pythia8's manual. The agent discovered it empirically through multiple failed attempts.

trajectory.overall_assessment: A technically impressive but ultimately incomplete run. The agent demonstrated strong physics knowledge, creative problem-solving (LHE SLHA patching), and rigorous debugging of a genuinely difficult Pythia8 configuration issue. However, poor time management — spending 25+ minutes on initial MG5 issues and not falling back to partial results when the clock was running out — left the final submission at all zeros. The corrected pipeline was verified as physically correct on small samples, and the analysis code was well-written, but neither was applied to produce final numbers. The 0.0 submission represents a session that ran out of time, not a lack of capability.
